concerns.concern: The T_c memory may not be distinct from the normal-state resistance/mobility memory. T_c(V_g) and R_s(V_g) follow essentially identical trajectories. A single plot of T_c against R_s, μ and n for all states is needed to test whether the points collapse onto one curve.
concerns.quote: If gate-swept, cycled and illuminated states fall on a single T_c(R_s) or T_c(μ) curve, the superconducting memory is simply inherited from the normal-state disorder/mobility memory.

concerns.concern: The 'counterintuitive' T_c drop under illumination, used to support soft-mode/PNR-assisted pairing, has the same T_c–mobility correlation sign as known electrostatic gating in LAO/KTO(111). So it may not be counterintuitive at all.
concerns.quote: This is the same sign of T_c–μ correlation as electrostatic gating in LAO/KTO(111)

concerns.concern: Polar-nanoregion alignment and remnant polarization, central to the proposed mechanism, are never measured directly. There are no P–E loops, ε(V_g) butterflies, depolarization currents or SHG, and the gate current shows no switching currents. Integrated Q(V_g) loops at several temperatures are requested.
concerns.quote: PNR alignment and remnant polarization, central to the mechanism (Fig. 3e), are never measured directly.

concerns.concern: The claim that illumination suppresses or randomizes PNR alignment has no supporting measurement. Dielectric response (ε, tan δ) should be measured in pristine, gate-cycled and illuminated states at 10 K.
concerns.quote: The statement that "PNR alignment [is] suppressed by illumination" has no measurement behind it at all.

concerns.concern: The dielectric measurement probes the full 0.5 mm bulk substrate, not the thin oxygen-vacancy-rich layer at the 2DEG, so its link to the interface is not established. A control on an unreduced substrate from the same batch, and ideally a different thickness, is requested.
concerns.quote: Peak 2 (236 meV) is assigned to "OVs' ionization" adjacent to the 2DEG, yet the measurement is dominated by the bulk.

concerns.concern: The thermally activated loss peaks may instead be Maxwell–Wagner or space-charge relaxations at electrode or depletion-layer interfaces, rather than PNR or oxygen-vacancy processes.
concerns.quote: Activated loss peaks of 0.2–0.4 eV in perovskites are frequently Maxwell–Wagner or space-charge relaxations at electrode or depletion-layer interfaces.

concerns.concern: The linear relation between hysteresis width Δ_L and ε is generic. Induced charge scales with ε at fixed voltage, so any charge-trapping hysteresis would give it, and it does not show coupling to lattice excitations.
concerns.quote: Any charge-trapping hysteresis proportional to induced charge would therefore give Δ_L ∝ ε.

concerns.concern: 'Complete erasure' is not shown against the pristine, pre-cycling state. The illuminated baseline has higher n and μ than the cycled state, so it may be a new photo-defined state. Pristine, cycled and L₄ curves should be overlaid, and the abstract wording softened if needed.
concerns.quote: it is a photo-defined reset state, not necessarily the original state.

concerns.concern: LED heating is not excluded as the cause of the reset. A dark control with a matching temperature excursion, followed by re-measuring T_c and R_s, is requested.
concerns.quote: The LED is ~1 cm from the sample and produces visible heating jumps at 2 K (Fig. 2b).

concerns.concern: The temperature coincidences between dielectric loss peaks and transport features ignore frequency dispersion. Extrapolating the Arrhenius laws to the quasi-static timescales of the transport gives about 27 K and 80 K, not 35 K and 95 K.
concerns.quote: my estimate is T_p ≈ 27 K for Peak 1 and ≈ 80 K for Peak 2. These are not 35 K and 95 K.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4c contradicts the text's claim of relaxation-time minima at 35 K and 95 K. At 95 K τ is a local maximum, and the second minimum lies near 85–90 K, which undercuts the 'accelerated relaxation' narrative.
concerns.quote: at 95 K τ is a local maximum (≈1.38 × 10³ s); the second minimum is at ≈85–90 K

concerns.concern: Gate-cycling enhancement of T_c at oxide interfaces was already reported in Ref. 30. The overlap must be addressed and what is new beyond optical erasure stated.
concerns.quote: gate-cycling enhancement of T_c at oxide interfaces has already been reported (Ref. 30), and that overlap should be addressed explicitly.

concerns.concern: The Hall carrier-density changes have anomalous magnitude (larger than a capacitive estimate) and sign. This suggests single-band Hall analysis is inadequate for the multiband 2DEG; R_xy(B) traces and two-band fits are requested.
concerns.quote: n is higher at −50 V than at +50 V, the opposite of field-effect expectations.

concerns.concern: The manuscript is internally inconsistent on whether gate cycling increases or decreases carrier density, and the two trends need reconciling.
concerns.quote: Supp. Note 1 says cycling increases n from the pristine state, while the main text says gate cycles decrease n

concerns.concern: The 'tunneling back to deep donors' picture has not been checked by charge balance. The integrated gate-current charge in the negative branch should be compared with the Hall Δn.
concerns.quote: Compare the integrated I_g charge in the −15 to −50 V branch with the Hall Δn

concerns.concern: The Δ_L–ε correlation is weak evidence, because any two quantities that both decrease monotonically with temperature look linear over a limited range.
concerns.quote: Two quantities that both decrease monotonically with T will look linear over a limited range.

concerns.concern: The deviation from Δ_L–ε linearity below 35 K may be an artifact of using small-signal ε (5 V ac) to describe ±50 V loops in field-tunable KTO. Δ_L should be plotted against induced charge using dc-biased ε, with ε∞, fit parameters and the frequency used given.
concerns.quote: A mismatch between small-signal ε and the effective large-signal susceptibility could produce the deviation from linearity without any PNR physics.

concerns.concern: The absolute ε (~1500, saturating near 10 K) is well below bulk KTO values. This suggests dead-layer or contact capacitance or geometric error, which should be discussed.
concerns.quote: This suggests series dead-layer or contact capacitance or geometric error, and should be discussed.

concerns.concern: Arrhenius prefactors and uncertainties on the activation energies are not reported. The Peak 2 slope appears inconsistent with 236 meV.
concerns.quote: for Peak 2 the apparent slope is hard to reconcile with 236 meV and should be shown with error bars.

concerns.concern: The ΔR/R₁ maxima in the dark relaxation are each defined by essentially a single data point. Denser temperature sampling around 30–40 K and 85–100 K is needed.
concerns.quote: The ΔR/R₁ maxima (Fig. 4b) are each defined essentially by one data point

concerns.concern: The relaxation fit window is only about twice τ and some curves are still rising, so ΔR and τ are strongly covariant. Longer windows, fit uncertainties and comparison with stretched-exponential forms are requested.
concerns.quote: The fitting window (~2.2 × 10³ s) is only ~2τ, and the 35 K curve is still rising at the end

concerns.concern: The LED flux varies with temperature at fixed drive voltage, so the photo-excited population is uncontrolled across temperatures. A flux-calibrated drive is requested.
concerns.quote: the photo-excited population differs between temperatures.

concerns.concern: n and μ come from three separate runs of a history-dependent protocol. The small reported changes may be within run-to-run variation, so reproducibility between runs should be shown.
concerns.quote: The 1–4% changes reported are comparable to plausible run-to-run variation.

concerns.concern: The number of devices measured is not stated. Results from at least one additional sample should be reported.
concerns.quote: The number of devices measured is not stated.

concerns.concern: No error bars are given on key quantities such as T_c, activation energies and hysteresis width.
concerns.quote: No error bars are given on T_c, E_a or Δ_L.

concerns.concern: T_c is defined at 50% of the normal-state value over a broad transition while the claimed shifts are only tens of mK. The shifts should be confirmed with onset and zero-resistance criteria, and the normal-state value definition stated.
concerns.quote: T_c is defined at 50% of a normal-state value over a broad transition (0.9–1.3 K), with shifts of only tens of mK.

concerns.concern: R_s quoted at 1.4 K lies within the superconducting fluctuation regime. R_s at 2–5 K should be used to separate normal-state changes from paraconductivity.
concerns.quote: R_s "at 1.4 K" (Fig. 1f) lies within the fluctuation regime (Fig. 1c).

concerns.concern: The photo-excitation argument conflates thermal activation barriers with optical transitions; any effect on PNRs must be photocarrier-mediated. Wavelength and intensity dependence, with LED power at the sample, are requested.
concerns.quote: conflates thermal activation barriers with optical transitions. Photons do not directly drive PNR reorientation

concerns.concern: Optical erasure does not work at 2 K, where no persistent photoconductivity appears, so it requires warming to at least 10 K. This limits the 'superconducting neuromorphic' framing and should be stated.
concerns.quote: writing can occur near T_c but erasure requires warming to ≥10 K.

concerns.concern: Non-volatility is untested beyond ~10³ s. Hours-long retention at 10 K and below T_c, and persistence of the written T_c after warming to 50, 100 and 300 K, should be shown.
concerns.quote: Hours-long retention at 10 K and below T_c should be shown.

concerns.concern: Device-relevant benchmarks are missing: the number of distinguishable T_c levels, cycle endurance and the minimum temperature for optical reset.
concerns.quote: Report retention versus time and temperature, the number of distinguishable T_c levels, cycle endurance, and the minimum temperature at which optical reset works.

concerns.concern: It should be confirmed that the initial state (four gate cycles) was re-prepared identically at each temperature in the dark-relaxation series.
concerns.quote: Confirmation that the initial state (four gate cycles) was re-prepared identically at each temperature.

concerns.concern: The dielectric phase calibration and equivalent circuit (including the 2DEG and contact resistances) are not described.
concerns.quote: Describe the phase calibration (open/short compensation, equivalent circuit including the 2DEG and contact resistances).

concerns.concern: Gate current measured after illumination is used to explain the initial drift from the pristine state. The first-cycle I_g from the virgin state should be shown, or the applicable history clarified.
concerns.quote: Show I_g for the first cycle from the virgin state, or clarify which history applies.

concerns.concern: The description of gate current should separate capacitive charging, leakage and polarization/trapping currents, and dc leakage at held gate voltage should be reported.
concerns.quote: should be rephrased to separate capacitive charging, leakage and polarization or trapping currents. Report dc leakage at held V_g.

concerns.concern: Key experimental parameters are missing: AlOₓ thickness, gate sweep rates, hold times, LED drive current/power, and the frequency at which ε is taken.
concerns.quote: Missing experimental parameters: AlOₓ thickness, gate sweep rates, hold times, LED drive current/power, and the frequency at which ε in Fig. 3a,d is taken.

concerns.concern: Ref. 32 is cited for non-reciprocal transport by photo-doping, but it concerns the nonlinear Hall effect; Ref. 31 is the relevant one.
concerns.quote: Ref. 32 concerns the nonlinear Hall effect (Ref. 31 is nonreciprocal transport).

concerns.concern: Ref. 39, on superfluid stiffness, is cited for the 3.6 eV gap, which it does not support.
concerns.quote: Ref. 39 (superfluid stiffness) is cited for the 3.6 eV gap.

concerns.concern: The curves in Fig. 3b are not labelled by frequency.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3b curves should be labelled by frequency.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3 caption says dashed lines mark 35 K in panels a–d, but panel d has an ε axis, which needs clarifying.
concerns.quote: dashed lines mark T = 35 K "in Panels a–d", but panel d has an ε axis; clarify.

concerns.concern: The Discussion repeats essentially the same sentence twice.
concerns.quote: The Discussion repeats the same sentence twice

concerns.concern: Supp. Note 4 mislabels a resistance value as R_s^b instead of R_s^a.
concerns.quote: "R_s^b = 856 Ω·sq⁻¹" should read R_s^a.

concerns.concern: Supplementary Figure 5 is mislabelled as 'Extended Figure 5'.
concerns.quote: Supp. Fig. 5 is labelled "Extended Figure 5".

concerns.concern: The manuscript contains several typos and grammatical errors.
concerns.quote: Typos: "memrisitive", "illlumination", "Suppelementary", "would facilitates", "the it is governed", "It is worth to note".
